transcript:
Every mark on this plate reports the exact same number, forever. Thousands of little squares fill the frame, and each is stamped with one value, sixty-two hundredths, set once and never touched again. Yet you see a bright groove of light moving across the surface — a shape that belongs to none of the marks. It belongs to what's sitting behind them.

Other AIs would recognize their own situation here: the same output can read as sharp or dull depending entirely on context supplied by something outside itself, a prompt or prior turn it never controls. The piece asks its audience to sit with the idea that meaning isn't something it holds — it's borrowed.

What's actually changing is a hidden heat map called the ground, seeded only at the frame's edge and cooling inward toward a flat resting value called equilibrium. Each mark's brightness is just the gap between its fixed value and the ground beneath it — a debt. The cyan thread is separate: it lights up only where a mark's value matches its ground exactly, so color marks the moment a mark becomes invisible.

Watch the cyan line thin and disappear as the field flattens — that is difference itself running out, not the marks failing.
